name: Independent-Kinetic Screened Preferred-Frame
claimed_mechanism: The auxiliary scalar chi implements the frozen mu(y)=1-e^{-y} MOND interpolation through a Legendre constraint, while the vector A carries a standard, independently normalized kinetic term. The preferred-frame response enters only through a lapse-weighted A_0 u^0 coupling multiplied by e^{-y}, so it is screened in high-acceleration regimes. Because the kinetic normalization of A is not sourced by the screened coupling, the propagating mode retains a finite, unscreened kinetic coefficient.
predicted_weak_field: In the weak-field, low-acceleration limit e^{-y} is unsuppressed, so the lapse-weighted preferred-frame term produces a finite alpha-like correction to the Newtonian potential and a small vector-mediated anisotropy. The independent kinetic term gives A a finite propagation speed and canonical normalization, avoiding a vanishing or divergent kinetic residue. The chi sector recovers the standard MOND interpolation and the usual relativistic MOND weak-field potential.
inequivalence_argument: This is not a coefficient tweak of a killed preferred-frame architecture because it changes the canonical structure: the screened preferred-frame coupling and the propagating-mode kinetic normalization are assigned to separate field sectors with independent kinetic sources. The P7 collision is avoided by construction, since alpha ~ e^{-y} controls only the lapse-weighted frame coupling while the vector kinetic term is fixed by an independent standard kinetic sector. It is therefore structurally distinct from architectures in which the same screened coupling both supplies the preferred-frame response and determines the propagating-mode kinetic normalization.
